clauses.current_legal_basis: The U.S. Code (release point 119-121, edition through 2026-10-09) prints EO 11446 as a note under 5 U.S.C. 7342, as amended by section 62 of EO 13286, with no ending statement; the bounded eCFR search as of 2026-10-14 and the Federal Register disposition-note search found no revocation or further amendment.
clauses.reason: The sole paragraph authorizes the Secretary of Defense and, for the Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy, the Secretary of Transportation to prescribe regulations for acceptance of medals and ribbons offered by multilateral organizations other than the United Nations, with State Department concurrence for service determinations. Before the amendment the Coast Guard officer named was the Secretary of Transportation; after section 62 of EO 13286 (effective March 1, 2003) it is the Secretary of Homeland Security, and the clause is otherwise unchanged. The clause continues as amended, the U.S. Code prints it as current, and it was operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
EO 11446 (Johnson, signed 1969-01-16, 34 FR 803, published 1969-01-18) authorizes the Secretary of Defense, for members of the Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps, and the Secretary of Transportation, for Coast Guard members when the Coast Guard is not operating as a service in the Navy, to prescribe regulations for the acceptance of medals and ribbons offered by multilateral organizations other than the United Nations in recognition of service under their auspices, with State Department concurrence for determinations about areas or purposes. Section 62 of EO 13286 (signed 2003-02-28, effective March 1, 2003 under its own section 92; held as an American Presidency Project transcription) strikes the Secretary of Transportation and inserts the Secretary of Homeland Security. The current U.S. Code (release point 119-121) prints the order as a note under 5 U.S.C. 7342, as amended by section 62 of EO 13286, with no ending statement. The order has no own-terms end, and the Federal Register disposition note lists only EO 13286. The order cites no statute as authority (it relies on the President's authority as President and Commander in Chief), so no authority statute needs checking.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end: the text sets no term or condition, and the only later instrument held that names the order is EO 13286 section 62, which substitutes one officer for another and does not revoke or supersede it.","independent_command_check":"The Defense authorization, the Coast Guard authorization and the State Department concurrence requirement belong to one sentence; the amendment changed only the identity of the Coast Guard officer, so none is separately ended.","savings_check":"No ending event, so no savings question arises.","scope_check":"Single operative scope: the whole sole paragraph, an authorization to prescribe regulations for acceptance of medals and ribbons from multilateral organizations other than the United Nations, with the State Department concurrence requirement."}

savings.reason: The order is a continuing authorization with no end and no savings clause; the only later change is the 2003 substitution of the Secretary of Homeland Security, which leaves the clause in force, so there is no residual beyond the operative clause itself.
